key_insight: Generalization of quantum policies and value functions is driven more by the circuit’s Fisher effective dimension—amplified by entanglement—than by the raw number of trainable parameters.
engineering_relevance: For quantum reinforcement learning, entangling connectivity should be treated as a core complexity knob because it can improve expressivity while worsening generalization, even at fixed parameter count.
method: PAC-Bayesian analysis with the Fisher geometry of PQCs
Controlled comparisons holding trainable rotations fixed while varying entanglement
Partial-correlation checks to separate entanglement effects from training accuracy, readout, and optimizer choices
evidence_signal: Across supervised classification, contextual bandits, and value-function tests, entangled circuits showed larger train-test gaps and the Fisher-based bound correctly ranked circuits with the same parameter count; the effect also persisted on IBM Heron hardware.
watch_item: The strongest ordering is not always fully resolved in end-to-end multi-step policy learning, where high return variance can obscure entanglement effects.
paper_title: Entanglement as a Structural Complexity Axis: A PAC-Bayesian View of Generalization in Quantum Policies and Value Functions
